note: Not a model call for an answer: the CLI refreshes the OAuth token as a side effect of being run. Since BH-2561 haiku is gone: the direct OAuth refresh endpoint is tried first, and only when it fails does the CLI fallback run, through agent-call on stage canary with the model from the model_routes role auth.fallback, AGENT_CALL_RUNNERS=claude and AGENT_CALL_LANE=oauth-refresh. The direct path is inert while OAUTH_REFRESH_CLIENT_ID is empty (its registry default), and then every refresh is the priced CLI fallback. Dedup-before-spend: it returns early unless the token is inside its expiry margin, and then the CLI fallback runs only after a canary-inference claim (cred_inference_claim oauth-refresh login:<12hex of the credentials file>) succeeds, so a dead login costs one call a day, not one per tick (BH-3222). That failed call is written row_source=unbilled and runs with AGENT_CALL_DEAD_ALERT=0, so it neither counts as unpriced nor pages DEAD. The census lane is null because oauth-refresh is a knob lib (catalog/lanes.d/_lib.oauth-refresh.json), not a registry lane, so bin/lib/llm-gate.sh finds no cap row for it and lets the call through. With no lane, the LLM sites screen attributes to this row every cost row on stage canary, including the lane-probe and claude-auth-check inferences, so its spend there is overstated and the row shows as shared.
